taxi_frames = []

    taxi_frames.append(monthly_df)

taxi = pd.concat(taxi_frames, ignore_index=True)

taxi = taxi[(taxi['passenger_count'] >= 1) & (taxi['passenger_count'] <= 6)]

In [59]:
print("The model explains around 84% of the variation since R^2 stands at 0.838. This means that the price is predicatable to a high extent from a handful of trip characteristics. More specifically, it shows that each additional mile (trip_distance) is associated with an, on average, 4.28$ increase in the total bill. This is not surprising. At the same time, it shows that each additional minute for the trip is associated with an increase of 0.14$. This is a bit surprising for myself, as I assumed the correlation would be a bit higher. Each additional passenger is associated with an increase of 0.77$. However, we know that cabs do not charge extra per person, so this might be an indirect data point showing that larger groups may take longer and more distant trips. A surprising data point is the fact that using a credit card averages 3.51$ more than using cash.")

The model explains around 84% of the variation since R^2 stands at 0.838. This means that the price is predicatable to a high extent from a handful of trip characteristics. More specifically, it shows that each additional mile (trip_distance) is associated with an, on average, 4.28$ increase in the total bill. This is not surprising. At the same time, it shows that each additional minute for the trip is associated with an increase of 0.14$. This is a bit surprising for myself, as I assumed the correlation would be a bit higher. Each additional passenger is associated with an increase of 0.77$. However, we know that cabs do not charge extra per person, so this might be an indirect data point showing that larger groups may take longer and more distant trips. A surprising data point is the fact that using a credit card averages 3.51$ more than using cash.
